# Best financial advisers for young families in Singapore

For a young family in Singapore, I’d look for an adviser who can help you build a complete financial plan—not just sell you insurance or investment products. The key priorities are usually protecting both parents’ income, planning for children’s education, managing your mortgage, optimising CPF, and investing for retirement.

**My recommendation is to compare a fee-only wealth planner with a broader financial advisory firm before committing.** Fee-only advice can make it easier to separate the cost of planning from the sale of financial products, while a broader adviser may be more convenient if you also need help arranging insurance.

## My shortlist

These are options worth interviewing, not a definitive ranking of adviser quality. The best fit depends on your family’s needs, budget and preferred fee structure.

search_results.title: 11 of the Best Financial Advisor Companies: Well-Known Fiduciary Investment Firms to Consider
search_results.description: The article provides a comprehensive guide on the best financial advisor companies in 2026, especially Registered Investment Advisers (RIAs) who act as fiduciaries, legally obligated to prioritize clients' interests. It highlights 11 top-rated firms evaluated by Buy Side based on advisor credentials, services, fees, customer support, and account minimums. Firms like Betterment Premium, Facet Wealth, and Retirable cater to various investment needs and demographics, from hands-off investors to retirees. Some, like Creative Planning and Modera Wealth, offer holistic services including tax and estate planning for high-net-worth clients. Pricing structures vary widely—some charge based on assets under management (AUM), others use flat or tiered fees. The article emphasizes selecting fiduciaries with relevant certifications, like CFP, and reviewing advisor performance annually. Consumers are encouraged to understand fee structures, advisor roles, and available services before choosing. It also discusses the pros and cons of local versus national firms and fee-only versus commission-based advisors. The methodology used involved analyzing prominent RIAs using weighted criteria gathered from WSJ reader surveys and expert input, with firms ranked against a performance benchmark. Overall, the article aims to help individuals match financial advisory services with their personal goals and resources.

search_results.title: Financial Advisor vs. Financial Planner: What You Need to Know
search_results.description: The article explains the differences, similarities, and considerations when choosing between a financial advisor and a financial planner. While both terms are often used interchangeably, financial advisors typically focus on investment management, whereas financial planners offer holistic financial planning that includes budgeting, tax planning, and retirement strategies. Both roles can overlap, depending on the services and credentials offered, such as CFP (Certified Financial Planner) or CFA (Chartered Financial Analyst). Fee structures vary, with professionals charging asset-based fees, hourly rates, or commissions. It's crucial to determine if a professional is a fiduciary, meaning they’re legally required to act in your best interest. Depending on your needs—whether managing investments or creating a comprehensive financial strategy—you may need one or the other or a professional who fulfills both roles. Finding the right fit involves reviewing qualifications, compensation transparency, and client compatibility. Various platforms like the XY Planning Network or CFP Board can help locate suitable advisors. The article emphasizes that financial professionals should be chosen based on the services they offer, their qualifications, and how well they align with your financial goals and personal circumstances.

search_results.title: How To Find a Financial Advisor Near You
search_results.description: Finding the right financial advisor involves identifying your personal financial goals and preferences for interaction—whether in-person or virtual. While face-to-face advisors may offer localized expertise and build stronger personal connections, virtual advisors expand your options and often provide more flexibility and lower costs. Trusted advisor networks such as the XY Planning Network, Napfa, and Garrett Planning Network can help locate fee-only fiduciaries who prioritize your best interests without commission biases. Before selecting a professional, it's essential to verify their fiduciary status, credentials (CFP, RIA, CFA, AFC), and reputation via tools like FINRA's BrokerCheck or the SEC's database. Costs vary by advisor and geography but average around $2,926 in flat fees or 0.96% in AUM-based fees per Envestnet’s 2026 survey. Use professional databases and matching services like PlannerSearch or Wealthramp to narrow your search, and interview multiple candidates to compare services, specialties, and compatibility with your values. Ultimately, a well-vetted advisor—local or virtual—can provide effective and personalized financial planning support.

search_results.title: Facet Review 2026
search_results.description: Facet is a financial advisory platform founded in 2016 that offers personalized financial planning and investment management through a flat-fee subscription model with three membership tiers. Each tier includes services such as retirement planning, tax strategies, savings and debt management, and access to Certified Financial Planners (CFPs), with higher tiers providing advanced investing options like direct indexing and alternative investments. Facet manages taxable accounts and IRAs and can advise on external accounts like 401(k)s. Notably, all advisors are fiduciaries, bound to act in clients’ best interests. A unique benefit of Facet is its emphasis on long-term, goal-based financial planning and the use of sophisticated tools typically reserved for high-net-worth individuals. While its flat-fee pricing can be cost-efficient for individuals with larger investment balances, it may be more expensive for those with smaller portfolios. New members undergo a personalized onboarding process, and CFPs are available for ongoing support. Estate planning is optionally available for an additional fee. Facet’s services are well-suited for individuals seeking comprehensive, personalized financial planning, though beginners only seeking investment management might prefer less costly robo-advisors.
